Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 1 and Part 35.15 of the
Regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the “Commission”),2 and
Order No. 714 regarding electronic filing of tariff submittals,3 Commonwealth Edison Company
(“ComEd”) submits this Notice of Cancellation of the executed Transmission Security Agreement
(“TSA”) by and between ComEd and Red Energy Partners LLC (“Red Energy” and collectively
with ComEd, the “Parties”) filed with and accepted by FERC in Docket No. ER26-841-000.4
ComEd is cancelling the TSA because the underlying retail service application has been cancelled.
In addition, since the Commission’s issuance of the September 18, 2026 order in Docket No.
ER26-3200-000, the Parties have mutually agreed to terminate the TSA. Accordingly, ComEd
respectfully requests that the Commission accept the Notice of Cancellation of the TSA,
effective October 27, 2026.

I.         BACKGROUND

       On December 19, 2025, ComEd filed the executed TSA between ComEd and Red Energy
pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act.5 The TSA was executed in connection with Red

II.         CANCELLATION OF THE TSA IS JUST AND REASONABLE

        In the September 18 Order, the Commission noted that while ComEd explained “that the
underlying retail service application ‘has been cancelled[,]’ [it did] not explain why cancelling the
Transmission Security Agreement is appropriate in light of the retail service application
cancellation, such as by identifying a provision of the Transmission Security Agreement to that
effect.”13 As indicated above, the TSA is fundamentally tied and inextricably linked to Red
Energy’s request for retail electric service to its proposed data center. Indeed, it exists to facilitate
a specific retail service request and guard against associated transmission-related risks. Here, the
underlying retail service application no longer exists. Because the TSA was executed solely in
connection with that now-cancelled retail service request, maintaining the TSA on file serves no
ongoing purpose. The Commission regularly accepts notices of cancellation of tariffs and service
agreements when the circumstances that justified them no longer exist, and the Commission should
do the same here.14

        Moreover, ComEd has a regulatory obligation to make this filing when proposing to cancel
the TSA,15 and the Commission has reminded jurisdictional utilities of the importance of their
filing obligations associated with rates and charges for jurisdictional services and all contracts and
agreements relating to such services subject to FPA section 205.16 Consistent with the
Commission’s filing requirements, the appropriate course is to remove from the tariff record
agreements that no longer correspond to an active service arrangement. Where, as here, the
underlying project has been abandoned and the agreement has no continuing function, cancellation
promotes an accurate and transparent Commission record. Under these circumstances,
cancellation of the TSA will simply remove from the Commission’s records an agreement
associated with a retail service request that is no longer being pursued, which is just and reasonable.

       Finally, and as indicated above, ComEd can now represent that the Parties have mutually
agreed to terminate the TSA, which serves as an independent ground for canceling the TSA.17

III.       PROPOSED EFFECTIVE DATE AND WAIVER

         ComEd respectfully requests that the Commission accept this Notice of
Cancellation, without suspension, hearing, or condition, effective October 27, 2026, the day after
this filing is submitted. ComEd requests waiver of the Commission’s 60-day prior notice
requirement to permit this effective date.18 Good cause exists to grant an October 27, 2026
effective date for the cancellation of the TSA. As indicated above, the underlying retail
service application has been cancelled and the Parties have agreed to terminate the TSA. Upon
cancellation of the agreement, the Parties will have no remaining obligations under the TSA.
No Parties will be affected or harmed by cancellation of the TSA, and ComEd has no need to
maintain the TSA on file with the Commission on and after the requested effective date. To the
extent any Commission regulation or other applicable requirements are not satisfied by this
filing, ComEd respectfully requests waiver of those requirements as well.

IV.        REQUEST FOR CUI//PRIV//HC TREATMENT

        Pursuant to section 388.112 of the Commission’s regulations,19 ComEd requests privileged
treatment for those portions of this filing that contain confidential information. The material
redacted from this filing contains sensitive information that if made public could competitively
damage the parties to the TSA. Such information constitutes “[t]rade secrets and commercial or
financial information obtained from a person [that are] privileged or confidential.”20 Accordingly,
good cause exists for the Commission to grant this request for privileged treatment of this
information.

        ComEd is hereby submitting a non-public version of this filing that contains the
confidential information. This version has been labeled “CUI//PRIV//HC” and should be made
subject to privileged document protection by the Commission.21 ComEd is also submitting a
public version of this filing with the confidential information redacted. This version may be placed
in the Commission’s public files.

       In accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 388.112(b)(2)(i), a proposed form of protective agreement
modeled on the Commission’s Model Protective Order is enclosed as Attachment C. To respect
the competitive concerns of its customer, ComEd has modified the protective agreement to provide

                                      PROTECTIVE AGREEMENT

        This Protective Agreement (“Agreement”), entered into this ___day of _______, 20_ by
and between Commonwealth Edison Company (“ComEd”) and ___________ (“Intervenor”),
shall govern the use of all Privileged, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or Critical
Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information (“CEII”) Material produced by ComEd to Intervenor,
or vice versa, in connection with the captioned proceeding before the Federal Energy Regulatory
Commission (the “Commission”). ComEd and Intervenor are sometimes referred to herein
individually as a “Participant” or jointly as the “Participants.”

     1. ComEd filed in the above-referenced proceeding Privileged Material, Highly Confidential
        Privileged Material, and/or CEII, as those terms are defined herein. Intervenor is a
        Participant in such proceeding, as the term Participant is defined in 18 C.F.R. Section
        385.102(b), or has filed a motion to intervene or a notice of intervention in such proceeding.
        ComEd and Intervenor enter into this Agreement to govern the use of Privileged Material,
        Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII produced by, or on behalf of, ComEd
        and/or Intervenor in the above-referenced proceeding. Notwithstanding any order
        terminating such proceeding, this Agreement shall remain in effect unless and until
        specifically modified or terminated by the Commission or a court of competent jurisdiction.
        In the event this Agreement terminates, the obligations of Reviewing Representatives to
        maintain the confidentiality of Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material,
        and/or CEII as provided hereunder shall remain in effect for 18 months following the date of
        termination.

     2. The Commission’s regulations 1 and its policy governing the labelling of controlled
        unclassified information (“CUI”) 2 establish and distinguish the respective designations of
        Privileged Material and CEII. As to these designations, this Protective Agreement provides
        that a Participant:

                  A. may designate as Privileged Material any material which customarily is treated
                     by that Participant as commercially sensitive or proprietary or material subject

       Certificate for Competitive Duty Personnel in the form attached hereto. All executed Non-
       Disclosure Certificates must be served on all Participants on the official service list
       maintained by the Secretary of the Commission for the proceeding.

    10. Any Reviewing Representative may, consistent with the requirements in Paragraph 3(G),
        disclose Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII to any
        other Reviewing Representative as long as both Reviewing Representatives have executed a
        Non-Disclosure Certificate. In the event any Reviewing Representative to whom Privileged
        Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII are disclosed ceases to
        participate in this proceeding, or becomes employed or retained for a position that renders him
        or her ineligible to be a Reviewing Representative under Paragraph 3(F) of this Protective
        Agreement, access to such materials by that person shall be terminated. Even if no longer
        engaged in this proceeding, every person who has executed a Non-Disclosure Certificate shall
        continue to be bound by the provisions of this Protective Agreement and the Non-Disclosure
        Certificate for as long as the Protective Agreement is in effect. 8

    11. All Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII in this
        proceeding filed with the Commission, submitted to the Presiding Judge, or submitted to any
        Commission personnel, must comply with the Commission’s Notice of Document Labelling
        Guidance for Documents Submitted to or Filed with the Commission or Commission Staff.9
        Consistent with those requirements:

                 A. Documents that contain Privileged Material must include a top center header
                    on each page of the document with the following text: CUI//PRIV or

7
    During this three-day period, a Participant may file an objection with the Presiding Judge or the Commission
    contesting that an individual qualifies as a Reviewing Representative, and the individual shall not receive access
    to the Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII until resolution of the dispute.

                CUI//PRIV//HC for Highly Confidential Privileged Material.                   Any
               corresponding electronic files must also include this text in the file name.

           B. Documents that contain CEII must include a top center header on each page of
              the document with the following text: CUI//CEII. Any corresponding
              electronic files must also include this text in the file name.

           C. Documents that contain both Privileged Material and CEII must include a top
              center header on each page of the document with the following text:
              CUI//CEII/PRIV. Any corresponding electronic files must also include this text
              in the file name.

           D. The specific content on each page of the document that constitutes Privileged
              Material and/or CEII must also be clearly identified. For example, lines or
              individual words or numbers that include both Privileged Material and CEII
              shall be prefaced and end with “BEGIN CUI//CEII/PRIV” and “END
              CUI//CEII/PRIV”.

12. If any Participant desires to include, utilize, or refer to Privileged Material (or Highly
    Confidential Privileged Material) or information derived from Privileged Material (or Highly
    Confidential Privileged Material) in testimony or other exhibits during the hearing in this
    proceeding in a manner that might require disclosure of such materials to persons other than
    Reviewing Representatives, that Participant first must notify both counsel for the disclosing
    Participant and the Presiding Judge (or the Commission), and identify all such Privileged
    Material (or Highly Confidential Privileged Material). Thereafter, use of such Privileged
    Material (or Highly Confidential Privileged Material) will be governed by procedures
    determined by the Presiding Judge (or the Commission).

13. Nothing in this Protective Agreement shall be construed as precluding any Participant from
    objecting to the production or use of Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged
    Material, and/or CEII on any appropriate ground.

14. Nothing in this Protective Agreement shall preclude any Participant from requesting the
    Presiding Judge (or the Chief Judge in the Presiding Judge’s absence or where no presiding
    judge is designated), the Commission, or any other body having appropriate authority, to find
    this Protective Agreement should not apply to all or any materials previously designated
    Privileged Material (or Highly Confidential Privileged Material) pursuant to this Protective
    Agreement. The Presiding Judge (or the Chief Judge in the Presiding Judge’s absence or where
    no presiding judge is designated), the Commission, or any other body having appropriate
    authority may alter or amend this Protective Agreement as circumstances warrant at any time
    during the course of this proceeding.

15. Each Participant governed by this Protective Agreement has the right to seek changes in it as
    appropriate from the Presiding Judge (or the Chief Judge in the Presiding Judge’s absence or
    where no presiding judge is designated), the Commission, or any other body having appropriate
    authority.


                                             7
 16. Subject to Paragraph 17, the Presiding Judge (or the Chief Judge in the Presiding Judge’s
    absence or where no presiding judge is designated), or the Commission shall resolve any
    disputes arising under this Protective Agreement pertaining to Privileged Material (or
    Highly Confidential Privileged Material) according to the following procedures. Prior to
    presenting any such dispute to the Presiding Judge, the Chief Judge or the Commission,
    the Participants to the dispute shall employ good faith best efforts to resolve it.

           A. Any Participant that contests the designation of material as Privileged Material
              (or Highly Confidential Privileged Material) shall notify the Participant that
              provided the Privileged Material (or Highly Confidential Privileged Material)
              by specifying in writing the material for which the designation is contested.

           B. In any challenge to the designation of material as Privileged Material (or Highly
              Confidential Privileged Material), the burden of proof shall be on the Participant
              seeking protection. If the Presiding Judge, the Chief Judge, or the Commission
              finds that the material at issue is not entitled to the designation, the procedures of
              Paragraph 17 shall apply.

           C. The procedures described above shall not apply to material designated by a
              Participant as CEII. Material so designated shall remain subject to the
              provisions of this Protective Agreement, unless a Participant requests and
              obtains a determination from the Commission’s CEII Coordinator that such
              material need not retain that designation.

17. The designator will have five (5) days in which to respond to any pleading requesting
    disclosure of Privileged Material (or Highly Confidential Privileged Material). Should the
    Presiding Judge, the Chief Judge, or the Commission, as appropriate, determine that the
    information should be made public, the Presiding Judge, the Chief Judge, or the
    Commission will provide notice to the designator no less than five (5) days prior to the date
    on which the material will become public. This Protective Agreement shall automatically
    cease to apply to such material on the sixth (6th) calendar day after the notification is made
    unless the designator files a motion with the Presiding Judge, the Chief Judge, or the
    Commission, as appropriate, with supporting affidavits, demonstrating why the material
    should continue to be privileged. Should such a motion be filed, the material will remain
    confidential until such time as the interlocutory appeal or certified question has been
    addressed by the Motions Commissioner or the Commission, as provided in the
    Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.714 and 385.715. No Participant waives its
    rights to seek additional administrative or judicial remedies after a Presiding Judge or Chief
    Judge decision regarding Privileged Material (or Highly Confidential Privileged Material)
    or the Commission’s denial of any appeal thereof or determination in response to any
    certified question. The provisions of 18 C.F.R. §§ 388.112 and 388.113 shall apply to any
    requests under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) for Privileged Material (or
    Highly Confidential Privileged Material) and/or CEII in the files of the Commission.

18. Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII shall remain
    available to Participants until the later of 1) the date an order terminating this proceeding no
    longer is subject to judicial review, or 2) the date any other Commission proceeding relating

                                               8
    to the Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII is concluded
   and no longer subject to judicial review. After this time, the Participant that produced the
   Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII may request (in
   writing) that all other Participants return or destroy the Privileged Material, Highly
   Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII. This request must be satisfied with within
   fifteen (15) days of the date the request is made. However, copies of filings, official transcripts
   and exhibits in this proceeding containing Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged
   Material, or Notes of Privileged Material, may be retained if they are maintained in accordance
   with Paragraph 5 of this Protective Agreement. If requested, each Participant also must submit
   to the Participant making the request an affidavit stating that to the best of its knowledge it has
   satisfied the request to return or destroy the Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged
   Material, and/or CEII. To the extent Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged
   Material, and/or CEII are not returned or destroyed, they shall remain subject to this Protective
   Agreement.

19. Regardless of any order terminating this proceeding, this Protective Agreement shall
    remain in effect until specifically modified or terminated by the Presiding Judge, the Chief
    Judge, or the Commission. All CEII designations shall be subject to the “[d]uration of the
    CEII designation” provisions of 18 C.F.R. § 388.113(e).

20. Any violation of this Protective Agreement and of any Non-Disclosure Certificate executed
    hereunder shall constitute a violation of an order of the Commission.
